chunks: From him, from Al-Hasan ibn Musa al-Khashshab, from Ghiyath ibn Kalub, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father (peace be upon him).

That a man sued Ali (peace be upon him) against another man, saying, 'He fabricated [a false claim] against me.' Ali (peace be upon him) said to the man, 'Did you do what you did?' He said, 'No.' Then Ali (peace be upon him) said to the plaintiff, 'Do you have evidence?' He said, 'I have no evidence.' Ali (peace be upon him) said, 'Then make him swear an oath for you.' The plaintiff said, 'Make him swear for me.' Ali (peace be upon him) said, 'There is no oath upon him [i.e., he is not required to swear].'

key_terms.اِسْتَعْدَى: Sued or brought a legal case

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling when a plaintiff has no evidence in Islamic jurisprudence according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates Imam Ali’s (peace be upon him) application of the principle of *al-bayyinah 'ala al-mudda'i* (proof is upon the claimant) in a scenario where the plaintiff lacked evidence. Notably, Ali ruled that the defendant did not need to swear an oath (*yamin*) to clear himself, distinguishing this case from others where an oath is required to resolve doubt, thereby emphasizing the rigor of evidentiary standards in Shia jurisprudence.
